answer: The spiral detector writes to velvet, and basalt publishes every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 281 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 135 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 39 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
